page: Microsoft Azure D64lds_v7 is an x86_64 instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor that delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 480 MB of L3 cache. The instance features a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM configuration with 128.0 GB of memory, resulting in 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly into the host with 3,780 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, while dedicated hardware GPU accelerators are not present.

In synthetic benchmarks, the D64lds_v7 achieves a PassMark CPU score of 83,685.33, placing it within the top 10 percent of tested servers. Multi-core performance is reinforced by strong stress-ng throughput and robust uncached large-block memory bandwidth of 311.23 GB/sec for reads and 126.27 GB/sec for writes. The processor architecture includes support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, reflected in high scores across cryptographic, compression, and physics benchmarks. At the application layer, the system delivered 109.21 million Redis SET operations per second and 87.37 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

By configuring 2 GB of memory per vCPU alongside 3.78 TB of local NVMe storage, the architecture trades heavy RAM density for compute and I/O efficiency. This profile minimizes excess memory allocation for tasks driven by raw clock speed and local disk operations. The server is well positioned for scale-out web serving tiers, Redis in-memory caching with fast local persistence, continuous integration build clusters, and high-throughput data ingestion pipelines.
description: The Microsoft Azure D64lds_v7 is an x86_64 server instance engineered for compute-intensive workloads requiring rapid local I/O. Powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor, it provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 480 MB of L3 cache, and 128.0 GB of system memory configured at a 1:2 core-to-RAM ratio. Bundled storage includes 3,780 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD capacity, with no GPU hardware attached. Benchmark results show top-tier PassMark compute performance and strong multi-core stress testing, supported by high memory bandwidth and integrated Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. High application throughput is evident in static web serving at 87.37 GB/sec and over 109 million Redis SET operations per second. The system is well matched for distributed caching, CI/CD compilation, and high-throughput database workloads.
